native.joinedText:
It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about routines; also, the use of adverbs of frequency is common on this topic.
ADVERBS OF FREQUENCY
100%
Always
We always work at night.
90%
Usually
She is usually late.
80%
Normally
They normally go to the beach on Saturdays
70%
Often
I am often at home.
50%
Sometimes
You sometimes laugh out loud.
30%
Occasionally
He occasionally cleans his room.
10%
Seldom
It seldom rains here.
5%
Hardly ever
Carol hardly ever takes a call.
0%
Never
John is never on time.
HINT

1. Adverbs go before verbs since they modify them, EXCEPT for To Be.
She is always happy

2. NEVER has a negative connotation. 
(no need for don’t/doesn’t)
They never visit me.

3. Adverbs can work in statements, negative sentences and questions.

texts: Talk about general actions everybody makes.
Talk about specific actions each one does.
Ruth changes Peter’s clothes  twice a day.
Talk about activities with specific time of occurrence.
Ruth has English class at 6 pm
When we talk about daily routines there are three main aspects that we should take into account using the simple present tense.

The three aspects talk about the same function but they aim different targets in language. The second aspect, as seen in the example, uses mainly general or indefinite time expressions to differentiate itself from the third one.
